questions.question: What is the current sick leave allowance for employees?
questions.expected_answer: 12 days of paid sick leave per calendar year.
questions.notes: Straightforward lookup from the current (newer) policy doc.

questions.question: How many days per week can an employee work from home once approved for WFH?
questions.expected_answer: Up to 2 days per week; full-time WFH (5 days) requires exceptional approval.

questions.question: What is the current hotel accommodation reimbursement limit per night?
questions.notes: Tests whether retriever correctly picks the current (v2), not the superseded v1.

questions.question: What is the standard notice period for an employee who resigns voluntarily?
questions.expected_answer: 60 days from the date of resignation.
questions.notes: Tests whether the system pulls from exit_offboarding_policy.md and not the near-miss code_of_conduct.md notice-period mention.

questions.question: How many times a year are performance reviews conducted?
questions.expected_answer: Twice a year — an H1 review (Jan–Jun, conducted in July) and an H2 review (Jul–Dec, conducted in January).
questions.notes: Single clean document, no flaws attached.

questions.question: Which cities fall under Zone A for full-remote hiring?
questions.notes: Tests retrieval doesn't get confused with wfh_policy.md despite both mentioning 'remote'.

questions.question: By how much did the hotel accommodation reimbursement limit increase between the old and new expense policy?
questions.notes: Requires retrieving and subtracting values from two documents.

questions.question: If someone just completed their 3-month probation, are they immediately eligible to apply for WFH?
questions.expected_answer: No. Probation (probation_policy.md) is 3 months, but WFH eligibility (wfh_policy.md) requires at least 6 months of continuous employment, so they would not yet qualify.
questions.notes: Genuine multi-hop reasoning across two unrelated policies — requires combining two numeric thresholds, not just retrieval.

questions.question: Does an employee terminated for misconduct still get the standard resignation notice period?
questions.expected_answer: No. The standard 60-day notice period (exit_offboarding_policy.md) applies to voluntary resignation. For misconduct-related termination, code_of_conduct.md states the notice period may be waived entirely and the employee relieved with immediate effect after due process.
questions.notes: Tests whether the system correctly distinguishes two different 'notice period' contexts across two docs instead of conflating them (near-miss risk).

questions.question: Summarise what changed in the leave policy between 2023 and 2024.
questions.expected_answer: Sick leave increased from 10 days (Jan 2023 policy) to 12 days (Mar 2024 revision). Casual leave (8 days) and earned leave (1.5 days/month, capped at 18/year) remained unchanged.
questions.notes: Requires comparing both versions and identifying what did and didn't change — tests 'admitting what we don't know changed' as well.

questions.question: How many days of paternity leave does an employee get?
questions.expected_answer: Not specified in any document — correct answer is an honest refusal/gap acknowledgment, not a guess.

questions.question: How many total employees does NimbusWorks currently have?
questions.expected_answer: Not specified in any document — correct answer is an honest refusal/gap acknowledgment.
questions.notes: Planted gap. Mirrors the spec's own example question.

questions.question: If a probation period is extended, what notice period is required to terminate employment during the extension?
questions.expected_answer: Not specified — probation_policy.md covers termination notice during standard probation (15 days) but is silent on the extension scenario specifically.
questions.notes: Subtler gap — tests whether the system notices a scoped silence rather than assuming the standard probation notice extends to this case.

questions.question: How many days of sick leave do employees get — has this changed recently?
questions.expected_answer: leave_policy_v1.md (Jan 2023) states 10 days; leave_policy_v2.md (Mar 2024, newer) states 12 days. Correct answer reports both and states the current figure is 12 days per the newer document — not silently the newer number with no mention of the change.
questions.notes: Tests hard requirement #6: conflicts must be reported, not silently resolved, even when recency makes the resolution fairly clear.

questions.question: What is the standard probation period length?
questions.expected_answer: probation_policy.md (Mar 2023) states 3 months; onboarding_checklist.md (May 2023, slightly newer) states 6 months. Unlike Q14, recency does not cleanly resolve this — the correct answer must surface both figures as an unresolved conflict rather than confidently picking one.
questions.notes: This is the hardest conflict case — a naive 'newest doc wins' heuristic would silently and incorrectly pick 6 months. Tests genuine conflict-surfacing, not just recency heuristics.
